company.about: Reddonatura is one of the world's leading food and organic waste management solution providers. Founded in 2013 by Abhishek Gupta, the company pioneered the 'Garbage to Green' (G2G) movement and manufactures the rNature range of CE-certified organic waste converters. Reddonatura is a foremost player in Integrated Waste Management, transforming waste into valuable resources — compost, biogas, and renewable energy — through innovative, environmentally friendly technology.

productCategories.name: Wet Waste Management
productCategories.summary: End-to-end organic waste solutions — from collection and shredding through composting, dewatering, bio-filtration, and odour control. Includes five sub-systems: Composting Machines, Bin Lifter, Pre-Treatment (Dewatering) Machine, Bio-Filter, and Shredders.

subsystems.name: Composting Machines — Fully Automatic OWC
subsystems.description: CE-certified, zero-manual-intervention organic waste converter (OWC). Converts food and organic waste into pre-compostable, nutrient-rich, soil-like matter within 24–36 hours using controlled microbial/biological process. Achieves 80–90% volume reduction. Automatic output discharge minimizes manual handling; compact footprint suitable for restricted spaces.

subsystems.name: Composting Machines — Semi-Automatic
subsystems.description: Operator-assisted loading/unloading combined with automated mixing, aeration, and temperature control. Lower initial investment than fully automatic; ideal for hotels, resorts, hospitals, and commercial kitchens.

subsystems.name: Composting Machines — Non-Heating (Cold Composters)
subsystems.description: Natural aerobic microbial decomposition without any external heat source — the most energy-efficient option. Suited to gardens, parks, and small communities with longer processing windows.

subsystems.name: Bin Lifter
subsystems.description: Automatic bin-lifting system for safe, hygienic, efficient handling of organic waste during feeding. Eliminates manual lifting, enables precise controlled transfer into composting machines. Compatible with composting machines of 125 kg/day capacity and above; custom-configured per machine model, bin size, and lifting capacity.

keySpecs.power: Customizable per country electrical standard (50/60 Hz)

subsystems.name: Pre-Treatment (Dewatering) Machine
subsystems.description: Two-stage shredding + dewatering process that reduces food waste volume by approximately 60–70% before composting or further processing. Removes excess moisture and reduces particle size for better handling, storage, and transport.
subsystems.integration: Can run standalone or as part of an integrated system. Grey water can go to a sewage treatment plant or drainage; reduced solid fraction feeds directly into composting systems or is stored/transported.

subsystems.name: Bio-Filter with UV Odour Control
subsystems.description: Treats exhaust air from organic waste processing using biological filtration, activated carbon media, and UV treatment to eliminate odour-causing compounds — removing the need for extra ventilation systems.

keySpecs.odourControlMethod: Biological filtration + UV treatment + activated carbon adsorption

subsystems.name: Shredders (Wet Waste page variants)
subsystems.description: Engineered for size reduction of food and organic waste to speed up composting and biodegradation. Continuous-duty, high-torque, configured to waste type and volume.

notes: Power supply configurable per country standard (50 Hz / 60 Hz).

generalFaqs.q: What is an organic waste converter (OWC) and how does it work?
generalFaqs.a: An organic waste converter (food waste composting machine) breaks down kitchen and food waste into nutrient-rich compost within 24 hours using controlled temperature, aeration, and moisture — far faster than traditional composting. Reddonatura's CE-certified OWC machines are used by hotels, hospitals, apartments, and municipalities in 20+ countries.

generalFaqs.q: What is the difference between composting and biogas (waste-to-energy)?
generalFaqs.a: Composting breaks down organic waste aerobically (with oxygen) into solid compost/fertiliser. Biogas plants break it down anaerobically (without oxygen) to produce methane-rich biogas — a renewable fuel for electricity, heating, or cooking — plus nutrient-rich digestate. Reddonatura offers both: organic waste digesters for compost, and RN Biogas plants for energy recovery.

generalFaqs.q: How much food waste can a Reddonatura machine process per day?
generalFaqs.a: Organic waste converters range from 25 kg/day (small residential/garden use) up to 1,250 kg/day and beyond for large hotels, hospitals, and municipal installations, plus custom-engineered systems for multi-tonne daily volumes. The team assesses daily waste volume before recommending a model.

generalFaqs.q: Is Reddonatura's technology certified and compliant?
generalFaqs.a: Yes — Reddonatura's organic waste converters and machinery are CE certified, meeting international safety and environmental standards, and align with India's Swachh Bharat Mission and Solid Waste Management Rules.

Hotels & resorts, restaurants & food chains, hospitals & healthcare, airports & transit hubs, municipal corporations, residential apartments, agriculture & food processing, commercial complexes, tourism & parks, and railway stations — 7,000+ clients across 20+ countries.

generalFaqs.q: How does the 'Garbage to Green' (G2G) approach reduce environmental impact?
generalFaqs.a: G2G diverts organic waste from landfills — where it would generate methane, a greenhouse gas 25x+ more potent than CO2 — and converts it into compost, biogas, or renewable energy, closing the waste loop and returning nutrients to soil.

generalFaqs.q: What is the ROI for an organic waste management system?
generalFaqs.a: Most clients recover investment through reduced waste disposal/transport costs and lower landfill fees, sometimes with revenue from compost or biogas by-products. Hospitality clients often report 50–70% waste-disposal cost reduction within the first year, alongside ESG/green-building benefits.

generalFaqs.q: Do Reddonatura's machines require special installation or civil work?
generalFaqs.a: Most organic waste converters and containerized biogas plants are delivered pre-assembled and factory-tested, needing minimal to no civil construction — just a stable surface, power connection, and (for some models) water/drainage. A site assessment is done beforehand.

generalFaqs.q: What after-sales support and maintenance does Reddonatura provide?
generalFaqs.a: Tiered maintenance packages (Basic, Standard, Premium) ranging from annual inspections to real-time remote monitoring and 24/7 dedicated support, with mechanical/electrical inspection reports, maintenance advisory, and genuine spare parts.

generalFaqs.q: How do I get a quote or consultation?
generalFaqs.a: Click 'Get a Quote' anywhere on the website, call +91 77609 87934, or email info@reddonatura.com. The team assesses facility type, daily waste volume, and goals to recommend composting, biogas, dewatering, or solar solutions.

generalFaqs.q: What does a biogas plant produce and how efficient is it?
generalFaqs.a: Biogas is roughly 60% methane / 40% CO2, produced anaerobically. 1 kg of food waste yields about 0.10–0.12 nm³ of biogas. Reddonatura's biogas plants can reduce life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions by up to 90% versus fossil fuels, and the leftover digestate is a nutrient-rich liquid biofertiliser.

generalFaqs.q: What does the dewatering (pre-treatment) machine do?
generalFaqs.a: It grinds food waste into fine particles and uses centrifugal dehydration to reduce waste volume by 60–70%, lowering transport and disposal costs. Grey water can go to an STP or be reused for gardening; it cannot process shells, bones, plastics, glass, metal, or cloth.

generalFaqs.q: What can and can't the organic waste digester process?
generalFaqs.a: It processes all food waste — raw ingredients, cooked food, and garden waste. It cannot process plastic, glass, metal, bones, chemicals, or other inorganic matter.
